thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=inference-queue-backlog severity=high threshold=5000 queue_depth=6243 -- https://pagerduty.example/services/inference-queue-backlog/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty: Trigger: inference-queue-backlog > 5000 for 3m. Affected region: us-west-2. Auto-escalation in 3m if unacked.

sam_w: oncall here, I'm looking. queue depth and retry storms?

jess_r: seeing steady increase in enqueued requests -> autoscaler not responding. `scale events` show no new nodes requested since 5m.

mike_t: confirm, `kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-worker` shows desired=50 current=50 but pods are in Pending due to node quotas.

sam_w: acked the PagerDuty incident (PD12345). Taking lead.

platform-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/inference/queue-backlog — recommended immediate actions: 1) check node pool quotas 2) attempt manual node group increase 3) throttle non-critical traffic.

ana_p: paging in since I'm on pager rotation standby. If node quota is hit, we may need manual spot pool bump or request on-call infra to increase node quota.

jess_r: Net new info: cloud provider reports instance quota at limit for account: compute.instances.core=200 (used=200). Autoscaler keeps queuing pods because no capacity to create nodes.

sam_w: ok, plan: (1) temporarily route low-priority customers to fallback model (smaller Llama-7B variant) (2) request manual quota bump from cloud console (3) if quota bump will take >10m, start manual surge with existing reserved nodes in eu-west-1 as stopgap.

mike_t: starting the fallback route now — updating router rules: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routes -d '{"route":"/generate","model_fallback":"llama-7b"}'` (will take ~30s to propagate).

jess_r: also throttling background batch jobs that are non-user-facing: applying rate-limit: `kubectl patch cronjob batch-precompute -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' -n prod`

platform-runbook-bot: Suggested command to manually increase nodepool (GKE example):
```
gcloud container node-pools update inference-pool \
  --cluster=prod-cluster --zone=us-west2-a --num-nodes=10
```

sam_w: I don't have quota to create those nodes. I've opened a cloud support quota request (https://console.cloud/quotas/REQ-789). ETA unknown.

ana_p: escalating to infra on-call (tagging @mike-infra). @mike-infra can you check org-level quotas?

mike_t: infra oncall (mike_t) here — confirmed org quota hit. I can temporarily free up some capacity by draining a staging pool and converting to prod, will take ~4-6m to cordon/drain and reprovision. Starting that now.

jess_r: meanwhile, can we change HPA target to be more aggressive to avoid oscillation once nodes become available? `kubectl edit hpa inference-worker` -> decrease target CPU from 60% to 50% and lower stabilization window.

sam_w: I'm leaving the HPA tweak to after nodes come up, we risk overscaling on burst. For now manual actions only.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PD12345 acked by sam_w at 4312345685. Next escalation if no resolution: 3m.

mike_t: staging pool conversion started — cordoning staging-nodes-1, draining pods (eviction). ETA 5m.

jess_r: Observability: error rate for /v1/generate jumped from 0.2% -> 4.6% and p95 latency up from 220ms -> 980ms over last 6m. Several customers reporting spikes in tail latency. Not yet widespread 5xxs but backpressure building.

sam_w: customer impact: narrow subset of production tenants in us-west-2 on hosted tier experiencing slowed responses; support already notified to triage VIP customers.

ana_p: good call on fallback model. Any logs showing KV cache thrashing?

jess_r: yes, KV cache hitrate down 12% on busy hosts. That makes smaller model fallback acceptable to reduce memory pressure.

platform-runbook-bot: If node drain route fails, fallback: reroute 30% traffic to dedicated-dhcp cluster in eu-west-1 via `traffic-split` with priority for enterprise customers.

mike_t: nodes are draining, new prod-capacity pool being created from drained nodes. kube events show new nodes registering now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation #1 -> ana_p triggered at 4312345760 (no longer time-limited due to manual actions).

sam_w: new nodes registered, pods scheduling again. Running `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep inference-worker | grep Pending` shows Pending count falling from 38 -> 6.

jess_r: routing propagation successful, fallback model serving started for low-priority tenants. Metrics show instant reduction in queue growth.

sam_w: mitigation summary: manual staging->prod node reassign + traffic fallback + paused batch jobs. Queue depth now 6243 -> 1870 and trending down. Latency p95 down to 420ms.

mike_t: confirming provider quota request still open; cloud support responded acknowledging request but no immediate quota increase. I'll follow-up with support escalation ticket.

ana_p: thanks all. I'll stay on for next 30m for post-incident notes and handoff. Sam, please create incident doc with timeline & customer impact and assign postmortem owner.

sam_w: will do. Postmortem owner: jess_r. Drafting now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD12345 resolved (manual) at 4312345980 by sam_w — incident closed.

mike_t: follow-ups: 1) request permanent quota increase 2) add autoscaler health-check to alert earlier (node allocation pending >2m) 3) add queue-length-based preemptive scale policy 4) run a chaos test for quota-loss scenario.

jess_r: postmortem items: evaluate fallback-model rollout automation, ensure routing tool supports per-tenant emergency throttles, and add guardrail that HPA won't stay silent when nodes can't be created.

sam_w: notes saved to incident doc https://incidents.redwood/PD12345 — closing thread. Thanks team :thumbsup:
